track.note: Centroid drift of a plume still attached to its source is slower than the air; direction is the main signal, speed is approximate.

per_plume.source_hint: unknown - no active volcanic or fire source; thin cloud/haze possible
evidence: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea WATCH/ORANGE but erupting=no, summit eruption paused with overflows stopped overnight; Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN erupting=no, so no active vog source. [E1]
No FIRMS fire clusters and no volcanic thermal in Hawaii box on 2026-09-09, arguing against wildfire smoke or active summit thermal. [E5]

Plume geometry far from vents: wind-based upwind end 430.8 km from Kilauea and 396.5 km from Mauna Loa, and tracked source end at 22.14N,-156.6E 333.4 km from Kilauea and 313.8 km from Mauna Loa; huge diffuse area 47904 km2 length 417 km over ocean. [E6, E3]

Motion disagrees with centroid wind: wind from 218 deg blows toward 38 deg (NE) at 33.3 km/h while plume drifted toward 283 deg (WNW) at 14.1 km/h, difference ~115 deg well outside 45 deg, lowering confidence in any transport story; fit R2 0.51 moderate. [E2, E3]

Winds variable: at tracked source end wind from 144 deg blows toward 324 deg within ~41 deg of drift, while at Kilauea summit wind from 188 deg blows toward ~8 deg (north), so northward transport is meteorologically possible but irrelevant without eruption. [E7, E3, E8]

Mask is 3.3% land over ocean but swallows Oahu (96% of Oahu covered) with Kauai fringe, so island cloud is included and mask is partly unreliable for a faint gray veil distinct from bright white cumulus/cirrus. [E4]

classify.caveats: Kilauea paused with Sept 8-10 episode forecast window so residual degassing cannot be fully excluded; mask swallows Oahu making island portion unreliable; drift vs centroid wind disagree strongly and tracking fit is only moderate.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Precursory overflows started yesterday afternoon, but stopped overnight during summit deflation. A forecast window of September 8-10 is likely for the start of episode 55.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts increased in August, while the summit region showed no other signs of deformation. Mauna Loa had an increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 87 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the August reporting period, after 57 in July. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
